home.title: {site}: agent skills compared
home.description: Web pages built by Codex and Claude Code with and without agent skills, side by side.
home.h1: What agent skills do to a web page
home.lead: The same prompts, built by Codex and Claude Code, each with and without a web-design skill (SKILL.md). Every prompt runs as a 2×2: Codex native, Codex + skill, Claude Code native, Claude Code + skill. The native cells are shared by all skills.
home.pending_hint: Cells that have not run yet show “Pending”.
home.overview_hint: Rows are skills, columns are prompts. Each square shows the Codex result on the left and the Claude Code result on the right (top of the page, desktop width).

method.table_note: The model and effort are fixed in the run scripts. The table shows what the run.json files record.
method.sample_title: One sample per cell, no picking
method.sample_body: Each cell is generated once, in one pass, with no follow-up turns. The result is shown as it came out, failed runs included. If a cell is rerun, the earlier attempt is kept in runs/<prompt>/_attempts/.
method.prompt_title: Same prompt in all four cells
method.prompt_body: The prompts use neutral wording with no style adjectives. Skill cells add one closing sentence that names the skill: Use the <name> skill. for Claude Code and Use the $<name> skill. for Codex.
method.isolation_body: Every run starts in a fresh throwaway directory outside the repository, with an empty HOME, its own config home (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME) and an environment built from scratch. No user settings, plugins, user-level skills, MCP servers or memories are loaded. The skill under test is copied only into that throwaway project's skill folder (.claude/skills/ or .agents/skills/). Skills bundled with each CLI stay available and count as native. The evidence comes from each agent's own logs and is stored in run.json under isolation.
method.fire_body: For skill cells, the logs must show that the skill was loaded (skill_triggered). If it was not, the cell is marked Failed instead of being shown as a skill result.
method.shots_body: Full-page captures at 1440 and 390 CSS px wide, taken after the network is idle and fonts have loaded, with animations disabled{tools}. Thumbnails show the top of the page. “Open page” loads the original index.html in a sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts", no same-origin access).
method.limit_native: Native means out of the box, not zero skills. Every cell, native ones included, can use the skills that ship with its agent: the 19 skills bundled with Claude Code, and Codex's system skills (imagegen, openai-docs, skill-creator, skill-installer). In the dashboard prompt, Claude Code's bundled dataviz skill fired on its own twice, once in claude__native and once in claude__frontend-design; run.json records this under builtin_skills_used. This is on purpose: the comparison is about what a reader actually gets after installing the agent.
method.limit_disk: Isolation means “nothing loaded”, not “nothing readable”. The agents can still read the rest of the disk: Codex's stock workspace-write sandbox can read /, and Claude Code with bypassPermissions has no sandbox. In the v0 runs, agents looked for AGENTS.md in parent directories and one used Playwright from the operator's npm cache. Stronger isolation (a separate user account or a container) is future work.
method.limit_fixed: Fixed sidebars in screenshots. Full-page captures draw position: fixed or sticky elements sized 100vh at the first screen's height only, so a dashboard sidebar can look as if it stops at 900 px. This comes from the capture, not from the page.
method.limit_once: One sample is not a benchmark. Each cell is a single generation. Treat the gallery as examples of what a skill tends to do, not as a score.
method.votes_body: Each result page has a 👍 vote through giscus, a third-party widget that loads only on result pages, not on the rest of the gallery. Voting needs a GitHub sign-in. Votes are stored as reactions in this repository's GitHub Discussions, one discussion per cell, shared by all languages. The counts on the comparison pages are refreshed every few hours. They show what visitors prefer; they are not an evaluation.
method.a11y_body: Each page is also checked with an automated accessibility scanner, and the number of violations by severity is shown. Automated scans catch only part of accessibility problems (they cannot judge, for example, whether alt text or focus order make sense), so treat the counts as a pointer, not a verdict.
method.video_body: Some cells also have a short recording of the page being scrolled at desktop width, because motion does not show in screenshots. It loads only when you press play on the cell page.

frontend-design.summary: Anthropic's official front-end design skill. It asks the agent to commit to a design direction (palette, type, layout, principles) and to check it against common AI defaults before writing code. Instructions only, no scripts.
notes: The same SKILL.md is also published in anthropics/claude-plugins-official and anthropics/claude-code; this gallery uses anthropics/skills.
Upstream rewrote this skill several times in 2026, so always use the pinned commit.

ui-ux-pro-max.summary: A community UI/UX knowledge-base skill: local CSV data (styles, palettes, font pairings, UX rules, chart types, stacks) plus a Python search script that produces a design system before the agent writes the page.
notes: Needs python3 (standard library only) to run its search scripts.
The upstream README recommends `npm i -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli`; the gallery uses npx with a pinned version instead, so nothing is installed globally.

web-design-engineer.summary: A front-end design skill whose output is always HTML (pages, dashboards, prototypes, slides, data visualization). It starts with a design-direction step and ships 25 style recipes. Instructions only, no scripts.
notes: Takes the place of OpenAI's frontend-skill in v0, because that skill was removed from OpenAI's official catalog and readers can no longer install it.
Its React path loads React and Babel from a CDN; the default hand-written CSS path needs no network.

landing-saas.title: SaaS landing page
landing-saas.summary: A marketing page for Rotaline, a fictional on-call scheduling tool: hero with a product illustration, features, steps, results, testimonials, pricing with a monthly/annual toggle, FAQ and footer.

dashboard.title: Data dashboard
dashboard.summary: A sales and operations dashboard for Kestrel Coffee Roasters: KPI cards, a monthly revenue chart with a channel filter, category shares, a sortable café table, recent orders and a stock warning, all from fixed data.

blog-portfolio.title: Personal blog and portfolio
blog-portfolio.summary: A one-page site for Maya Lindqvist, a fictional product designer: four case studies, a filterable post list, one full article, an about section with a timeline, a newsletter form and a light/dark switch.

form-states.title: Form and feedback component states
form-states.summary: A reference page for a fictional online bank’s form and feedback components, with every state visible at once: text fields, choices, buttons, a transfers list (loading, empty, error, filled), messages and a transfer form.
